analysis.title: Duttenhoefer's Daily (12.11.2026)
key_insights: S&P 500 rose 131bps to 7619 (+11% YTD), led by tech: NeoClouds +12%, SOX +6%, Retail Favorites +5%. Nasdaq is back above pre-election levels.
Systematic long/short managers were up 1.25%, a +2.6 SD move and their best day since June.
SOX touched its 200-day moving average. The note frames it as either a bear market bounce or a tradable mid-cycle correction.
Nvidia fell 8% after the market close on rumours of an internal affair.
Rates and macro levels cited: US 10-year at 4.99%, EUR/USD below 1.11 with the dollar modestly stronger on a hawkish Fed, Brent $93, Gold $3965, Bitcoin $74k.
Nebius reports today. Cisco and Applied Materials report tomorrow.
Fed: GS continues to expect a second 25bp hike in December and adds a third 25bp hike in March, which could come as early as January.

US capex: GS economists see 2026 as a strong capex year (+11%) and forecast real business fixed investment growth of 8% in 2027. AI stays the dominant driver, but official statistics will show a smaller impact than company spending data because most equipment is imported. Midterm results pose only modest risk to AI investment. Manufacturing facility spending is expected to decline and energy investment to rise.

Semis: GS believes the current drawdown is overdone. About 35 GW of 2027 datacenter deployments are already largely in progress, so execution risk is relatively low. NVDA and AVGO are at very attractive entry points, and AMAT and LRCX are particularly compelling.

Datacenter pipeline: GS sees about 35 GW of 2027 builds as relatively low risk, a 2028 floor of another 35 GW and up to 55-60 GW if projects proceed. Under-construction US net additions are 22/24/5 GW-IT for 2027/28/29 (1.5 PUE, Aterio data). US AI investment is estimated at $1.4tn annualized by end-2027.

Europe power: the EUDCA Secretary General says European datacenter development is unaffected by US midterms, the market could more than double by the early 2030s, and power grids are the single largest bottleneck.

Nike: a spec sales view says FY28 EPS is still too high and the 31x P/E is too high for a company with y/y revenue declines in 6 of the last 9 quarters. The current quarter is expected to be the worst decline (-10%) in almost 2 years.
US retail sales: Apollo's weekly consumer spending data stays strong, showing a significant gap between what consumers say and what they do.
Alibaba plans a Hong Kong listing of its chip design arm T-Head to raise $2-3bn. Alibaba claims a V900-powered cluster can link up to 500,000 chips for training and inference.

United Airlines is banning AI agents from making flight reservations on behalf of travellers, citing security risks and possible violation of federal rules. Similar headlines have appeared for bank transactions and other industries.
Chinese equities have failed to convert macro growth into returns since 2020 (6% EPS CAGR since 2021). GS projects 10% trend EPS growth and stays bullish on Stable and Cash Return Growth.
A quoted market view says money flow should be more favorable over the last eight weeks of 2026, but 2027 may see the largest increase in net supply since 2000.
